draft.title: Simplifying surds
card: A surd is a root that cannot be written as a fraction, so its decimal never ends or repeats. \(\sqrt{5}\) and \(\sqrt{12}\) are surds. \(\sqrt{9}\) is not, because it equals 3.
To simplify a surd, find the largest square number that divides the number under the root. Square numbers are \(4\), \(9\), \(16\), \(25\), \(36\) and so on.
Split the root using \(\sqrt{a \times b} = \sqrt{a} \times \sqrt{b}\). Then take the square root of the square factor and write it in front.
Example: \(\sqrt{50} = \sqrt{25 \times 2}\), which is \(\sqrt{25} \times \sqrt{2} = 5\sqrt{2}\). A number already in front is multiplied: \(3\sqrt{8} = 3 \times 2\sqrt{2} = 6\sqrt{2}\).
draft.remember: Pull out the largest square factor, and its square root goes in front of the surd.

a.why: Here \(72 = 36 \times 2\), and \(\sqrt{36} = 6\), so \(\sqrt{72} = 6\sqrt{2}\). The option \(3\sqrt{8}\) is equal in value but not simplest, because \(8\) still has the square factor \(4\).
a.clue: Find the largest square number that divides 72.

b.q: Mia says the diagonal of a square tile is \(\sqrt{48}\) cm. Which is this length in simplest form?
b.why: Here \(48 = 16 \times 3\), and \(\sqrt{16} = 4\), so \(\sqrt{48} = 4\sqrt{3}\). The option \(2\sqrt{12}\) used the square factor \(4\) only, so \(12\) can still be simplified.
b.clue: Check that no square factor is left under the root.
